subkeys.content: The common name of the server certificate. The system uses this name to validate the certificate sent by the IKE server. If not set, the system uses the remote identifier to validate the certificate.

subkeys.title: TLS Minimum Version
subkeys.content: The minimum TLS version to use with EAP-TLS authentication.

subkeys.title: TLS Maximum Version
subkeys.content: The maximum TLS version to use with EAP-TLS authentication.

subkeys.title: Use IPv4 / IPv6 Internal Subnet Attributes
subkeys.content: If `1`, negotiations should use IKEv2 Configuration Attribute `INTERNAL_IP4_SUBNET` and `INTERNAL_IP6_SUBNET`.

subkeys.title: Disable Mobility and Multihoming
subkeys.content: If `1`, the system disables MOBIKE.

subkeys.title: Disable Redirect
subkeys.content: If `1`, the system disables IKEv2 redirect. If not set, the system redirects an IKEv2 connection when it receives a redirect request from the server.

subkeys.title: Enable Disconnect on Idle
subkeys.content: If `1`, the VPN disconnects automatically after a period defined by `DisconnectOnIdleTimer`.

subkeys.title: Disconnect on Idle time
subkeys.content: Only used if `DisconnectOnIdle` is `1`. The number of seconds before the VPN disconnects. On watchOS, maximum allowed value is 15 seconds

subkeys.title: NAT Keep Alive Offload Enable
subkeys.content:
If `1`, enables NAT keepalive offload for Always On VPN IKEv2 connections. The device sends keepalive packets to maintain NAT mappings for IKEv2 connections that have a NAT on the path. It sends keepalive packets at regular intervals when the device is awake. If `NATKeepAliveOffloadEnable` is `1`, the system offloads keepalive packets to hardware while the device is asleep.

NAT keepalive offload has an impact on the battery life due to the extra workload during sleep. The default interval for the keepalive offload packets is 20 seconds over Wi-Fi and 110 seconds over Cellular interface. The default NAT keepalive works well on networks with small NAT mapping timeouts but imposes a potential battery impact. If a network has larger NAT mapping timeouts, larger keepalive intervals may be safely used to minimize battery impact. Modify the keepalive interval through the `NATKeepAliveInterval` key.

subkeys.title: NAT Keepalive Interval
subkeys.content: The NAT Keepalive interval for Always On VPN IKEv2 connections. This value controls the interval that the device sends keepalive offload packets. The minimum value is 20 seconds. If no key is specified, the default is 20 seconds over Wi-Fi and 110 seconds over a cellular interface.

subkeys.title: Enable perfect forward secrecy
subkeys.content: If `1`,  enables Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) for IKEv2 Connections.

subkeys.title: Enable certificate revocation check
subkeys.content: If `1`, the system performs a certificate revocation check for IKEv2 connections. This is a best-effort revocation check and server response timeouts won't cause it to fail.

subkeys.title: Enable fallback
subkeys.content:
If `1`, the system enables a tunnel over cellular data to carry traffic that's eligible for Wi-Fi Assist and also requires VPN.

Enabling fallback requires that the server support multiple tunnels for a single user.

This field is available in iOS 13 and later, and tvOS 17 and later. Not available in watchOS.

subkeys.title: Maximum Transmission Unit
subkeys.content: The Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) specifies the maximum size in bytes of each packet that the system sends over the IKEv2 VPN interface. Available in iOS 14 and later, and macOS 11 and later.

subkeys.title: ProviderType
subkeys.content: If the value of this key is `app-proxy`, the VPN service tunnels traffic at the application layer. If the value of this key is `packet-tunnel`, the VPN service tunnels traffic at the IP layer.

subkeys.title: Include All Networks
subkeys.content:
If `1`, then the system routes all network traffic through the VPN, with some controllable exclusions, such as `ExcludeLocalNetworks`, `ExcludeCellularServices`, and `ExcludeAPNs` properties. The system always excludes the following traffic from the tunnel:

- Traffic necessary for connecting and maintaining the device's network connection, such as DHCP.
- Traffic necessary for connecting to captive networks.
- Certain cellular services traffic that's not routable over the internet and is instead directly routed to the cellular network. See the `ExcludeCellularServices` field for more information.
- Network communication with a companion device such as a watchOS device.

subkeys.title: Enforce Routes
subkeys.content: If `1`, all the VPN's non-default routes take precedence over any locally-defined routes. If `IncludeAllNetworks` is `1`, the system ignores `EnforceRoutes`.

subkeys.title: Exclude Local Networks
subkeys.content: If `1` and either `IncludeAllNetworks` or `EnforceRoutes` are `1`, then the system routes local network traffic outside of the VPN. The default for this value is `0` on macOS and `1` on iOS.

subkeys.title: Exclude Cellular Services
subkeys.content: If `1` and `IncludeAllNetworks` is `1`, the system excludes internet-routable network traffic for cellular services (VoLTE, Wi-Fi Calling, IMS, MMS, Visual Voicemail, etc.) from the tunnel. Note that some cellular carriers route cellular services traffic directly to the carrier network, bypassing the internet. Such cellular services traffic is always excluded from the tunnel.

subkeys.title: Exclude APNs
subkeys.content: If `1` and `IncludeAllNetworks` is `1`, the system excludes network traffic for the Apple Push Notification service (APNs) from the tunnel.

subkeys.title: Exclude Device Communication
subkeys.content: If set to `1` and `IncludeAllNetworks` is set to `1`, the device excludes network traffic used for communicating with devices connected via USB or Wi-Fi from the tunnel.

subkeys.title: Post-quantum Pre-shared Key
subkeys.content: The Post-quantum Pre-shared key (PPK) the device uses for this VPN. This key is is used with VPN servers that support RFC 8784. If this key is present `PPKIdentifier` must also be present.

subkeys.title: Post-quantum Pre-shared Key Identifier
subkeys.content: The identifier for the Post-quantum Pre-shared key (PPK) the device uses for this VPN. This key is is used with VPN servers that support RFC 8784. If this key is present `PPK` must also be present.

subkeys.title: Post-quantum Pre-shared Key Mandatory
subkeys.content: If set to `1`, the VPN doesn't establish a connection if the server doesn't support RFC 8784 or doesn't accept the PPK identifier specified in `PPKIdentifier`. The device ignores this key if `PPK` and `PPKIdentifier` are not present.

subkeys.title: Allow Post-quantum Key Exchange Fallback
subkeys.content: If set to `0`, the VPN doesn't establish a connection if the server does not support or doesn't allow post-quantum key exchanges. Thd device ignores this key if `PostQuantumKeyExchangeMethods` is not present in `IKESecurityAssociationParameters` or `ChildSecurityAssociationParameters`.

subkeys.title: Enforce Strict Algorithm Selection
subkeys.content: If set to `1`, the device doesn't allow DES, 3DES, and Diffie-Hellman groups less than 14. Also the device requires the encryption algorithm specified for the IKE SA to be at least as cryptographically strong as the algorithm specified for the child SA. The device rejects this profile payload if these requirements are not met.

subkeys.title: IKESecurityAssociationParameters
subkeys.content: These parameters apply to Child Security Association unless `ChildSecurityAssociationParameters` is specified.

subkeys.title: EncryptionAlgorithm
subkeys.content:
The encryption algorithm.

In watchOS and tvOS, the default value is `AES-256-GCM`.
`DES` and `3DES` are available only in iOS, macOS, and visionOS prior to iOS 26, macOS 26, and visionOS 26.

subkeys.title: IntegrityAlgorithm
subkeys.content:
The integrity algorithm.

`SHA1-96` and `SHA1-160` are available only in iOS, macOS, and visionOS prior to iOS 26, macOS 26, and visionOS 26.

subkeys.title: DiffieHellmanGroup
subkeys.content:
The Diffie-Hellman group.

For `AlwaysOn` VPN in iOS 14.2 and later, the minimum allowed value is `14`.

`1`, `2`, and `5` are available only in iOS, macOS, and visionOS prior to iOS 26, macOS 26, and visionOS 26.

subkeys.title: Post-quantum Key Exchange Methods
subkeys.content: An array of strings representing postquantum key exchange methods the device uses during SA establishment and rekey. You can specify up to seven items, which correspond to ADDKE1 - ADDKE7 from RFC 9370.

subkeys.title: LifeTimeInMinutes
subkeys.content: The SA lifetime (rekey interval) in minutes.

subkeys.title: ChildSecurityAssociationParameters
subkeys.content: The `ChildSecurityAssociationParameters` dictionaries.

subkeys.title: EncryptionAlgorithm
subkeys.content:
The encryption algorithm.

In watchOS and tvOS, the default value is `AES-256-GCM`.
`DES` and `3DES` are available only in iOS, macOS, and visionOS prior to iOS 26, macOS 26, and visionOS 26.

subkeys.title: IntegrityAlgorithm
subkeys.content:
The integrity algorithm.

`SHA1-96` and `SHA1-160` are available only in iOS, macOS, and visionOS prior to iOS 26, macOS 26, and visionOS 26.

subkeys.title: DiffieHellmanGroup
subkeys.content:
The Diffie-Hellman group.

For `AlwaysOn` VPN in iOS 14.2 and later, the minimum allowed value is `14`.

`1`, `2`, and `5` are available only in iOS, macOS, and visionOS prior to iOS 26, macOS 26, and visionOS 26.

subkeys.title: Post-quantum Key Exchange Methods
subkeys.content: An array of strings representing postquantum key exchange methods the device uses during SA establishment and rekey. You can specify up to seven items, which correspond to ADDKE1 - ADDKE7 from RFC 9370.

subkeys.title: LifeTimeInMinutes
subkeys.content: The SA lifetime (rekey interval) in minutes.

keys.title: DNS
keys.content: A dictionary to use for all VPN types.

subkeys.title: DNS Protocol
subkeys.content: The transport protocol to communicate with the DNS server.

subkeys.title: Server URL
subkeys.content: The URI template of a DNS-over-HTTPS server, as defined in RFC 8484, which needs to use the `https://` scheme. The system uses the hostname or address in the URL to validate the server certificate. If `ServerAddresses` isn't specified, the system uses the hostname or address in the URL to determine the server addresses. This key is required if the `DNSProtocol` is `HTTPS`.

subkeys.title: Server Name
subkeys.content: The hostname of a DNS-over-TLS server to validate the server certificate, as defined in RFC 7858. If `ServerAddresses` isn't specified, the system uses the hostname to determine the server addresses. This key is required if the `DNSProtocol` is `TLS`.

subkeys.title: DNS Server Addresses
subkeys.content: The array of DNS server IP address strings. These IP addresses can be a mixture of IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.

subkeys.title: DNS Search Domains
subkeys.content: The list of domain strings used to fully qualify single-label host names.

subkeys.title: Domain Name
subkeys.content: The primary domain of the tunnel.

subkeys.title: Supplemental Match Domains
subkeys.content:
The list of domain strings used to determine which DNS queries use the DNS resolver settings in `ServerAddresses`. The system uses this key to create a split DNS configuration where it resolves only hosts in certain domains using the tunnel's DNS resolver. The system uses the default resolver for hosts that aren't in one of the domains in this list.

If `SupplementalMatchDomains` contains the empty string it becomes the default domain.

Split-tunnel configurations can direct all DNS queries to the VPN DNS servers before the primary DNS servers. If the VPN tunnel becomes the network's default route, the servers listed in `ServerAddresses` become the default resolver and the system ignores the `SupplementalMatchDomains` list.

subkeys.title: Supplemental Match Domains No Search
subkeys.content: If `0`, append the domains in the `SupplementalMatchDomains` list to the resolver's list of search domains.

subkeys.title: DNS Certificate UUID
subkeys.content: That UUID that points to an identity certificate payload. The system uses this identity to authenticate the user to the DNS resolver.

keys.title: Proxies
keys.content: The dictionary to use to configure `Proxies` for use with `VPN`.

subkeys.title: Proxy AutoConfig Enable
subkeys.content: If `true`, enables automatic proxy configuration.

subkeys.title: Proxy Auto Discovery Enable
subkeys.content: If `true`, enables proxy auto discovery.

subkeys.title: Proxy Server URL
subkeys.content: The URL to the location of the proxy auto-configuration file. Used only when `ProxyAutoConfigEnable` is `true`.

subkeys.title: Supplemental Match Domains
subkeys.content: An array of domains that defines which hosts use proxy settings for hosts.

subkeys.title: Enable HTTP
subkeys.content: If `1`, enables proxy for HTTP traffic.

subkeys.title: HTTP Proxy
subkeys.content: The host name of the HTTP proxy.

subkeys.title: HTTP Port
subkeys.content: The port number of the HTTP proxy. This field is required if `HTTPProxy` is specified.

subkeys.title: HTTP ProxyUsername
subkeys.content: The user name used for authentication.

subkeys.title: HTTP ProxyPassword
subkeys.content: The password used for authentication.

subkeys.title: Enable HTTPS
subkeys.content: If `true`, enables proxy for HTTPS traffic.

subkeys.title: HTTPS Proxy
subkeys.content: The host name of the HTTPS proxy.

subkeys.title: HTTPS Port
subkeys.content: The port number of the HTTPS proxy. This field is required if `HTTPSProxy` is specified.

keys.title: AlwaysOn
keys.content: The dictionary to use when `VPNType` is `AlwaysOn`. Not available in tvOS or watchOS.

subkeys.title: UI Toggle Enabled
subkeys.content: If `1`, allows the user to disable the VPN configuration.

subkeys.title: TunnelConfigurations
subkeys.content: An array that contains an arbitrary number of tunnel configurations.

subkeys.title: Protocol Type
subkeys.content: The type of connection, which needs to be `IKEv2`.

subkeys.title: Interfaces
subkeys.content: The interfaces to apply this configuration to.

subkeys.title: ServiceExceptions
subkeys.content: An array that contains an arbitrary number of service exceptions.

subkeys.title: Service Name
subkeys.content:
The name of a service that's exempt from Always On VPN.

`CellularServices` is available in iOS 11.3 and later; it exempts `VoLTE`, `IMS` and `MMS`. WiFiCalling is exempted in iOS 13.4 and later.

`DeviceCommunication` is available in iOS 17.4 and later; it exempts network traffic used for communicating with devices connected via USB or Wi-Fi.

subkeys.title: Action
subkeys.content: The action to take with network connections from the named service.

subkeys.title: ApplicationExceptions
subkeys.content: An array that contains an arbitrary number of apps whose connections occur outside the VPN.

subkeys.title: Bundle Identifier
subkeys.content: The app's bundle identifier.

subkeys.title: LimitToProtocols
subkeys.content: Limit the exception to only the specified list of protocols, with support for `UDP` only.

subkeys.title: Allow Captive Web Sheet
subkeys.content: If `1`, allows traffic from Captive Web Sheet outside the VPN tunnel.

subkeys.title: Allow All Captive Network Plugins
subkeys.content: If `1`, allows traffic from all captive networking apps outside the VPN tunnel to perform captive network handling.

subkeys.title: AllowedCaptiveNetworkPlugins
subkeys.content: The array of captive networking apps whose traffic is allowed outside the VPN tunnel, to perform captive network handling. Used only when `AllowAllCaptiveNetworkPlugins` is `false`.

subkeys.title: Bundle Identifier
subkeys.content: The bundle identifier for the app that's allowed on the captive network.

keys.title: TransparentProxy
keys.content: The dictionary to use when `VPNType` is `TransparentProxy`. Available in macOS 14 and later.

subkeys.title: Authentication Method
subkeys.content:
The type of authentication method to use: `Password`, `Certificate`, or `Password+Certificate`.

Available in macOS 14 and later.

subkeys.title: Enable Disconnect on Idle
subkeys.content:
If `1`, the VPN disconnects automatically disconnect after a period defined by `DisconnectOnIdleTimer`.

Available in macOS 14 and later.

subkeys.title: Disconnect on Idle time
subkeys.content:
The number of seconds before the VPN disconnects. This value is only used if `DisconnectOnIdle` is `1`.

Available in macOS 14 and later.

subkeys.title: Enforce Routes
subkeys.content:
If `1`, then all the VPN's non-default routes take precedence over any locally-defined routes. If `IncludeAllNetworks` is `1`, the system ignores the value of `EnforceRoutes`.

Available in macOS 14 and later.

subkeys.title: Enable VPN On Demand
subkeys.content:
If `1`, the system brings up the VPN on demand.

Available in macOS 14 and later.

subkeys.title: On Demand Rules
subkeys.content:
Determines when and how the system uses an OnDemand VPN.

Available in macOS 14 and later.

subkeys.title: On Demand Action
subkeys.content:
The action to take if this dictionary matches the current network. Possible values are:
- `Allow`: Deprecated. Allow VPN On Demand to connect if triggered.
- `Connect`: Unconditionally initiate a VPN connection on the next network attempt.
- `Disconnect`: Tear down the VPN connection and don't reconnect on demand as long as this dictionary matches.
- `EvaluateConnection`: Evaluate the ActionParameters array for each connection attempt.
- `Ignore`: Leave any existing VPN connection up, but don't reconnect on demand as long as this dictionary matches.
Only the `Disconnect` action is available on watchOS 10 and later.

subkeys.title: Action Parameters
subkeys.content: An array of dictionaries that provides rules similar to the `OnDemandRules` dictionary, but evaluated on each connection instead of when the network changes. This value is only for use with dictionaries in which the `Action` value is `EvaluateConnection`. The system evaluates these dictionaries in order and the first dictionary that matches determines the behavior. Not available in watchOS.

subkeys.title: Action Parameter
subkeys.content:
A dictionary that provides rules similar to the OnDemandRules dictionary, but evaluated on each connection instead of when the network changes. These dictionaries are evaluated in order, and the behavior is determined by the first dictionary that matches.
The keys allowed in each dictionary are described below. Note: This array is used only for dictionaries in which EvaluateConnection is the Action value.

subkeys.title: Domains
subkeys.content: The domains to apply this evaluation.

subkeys.title: Domain Action
subkeys.content:
Defines the VPN behavior for the specified domains. Allowed values are:
* 'ConnectIfNeeded': The specified domains should trigger a VPN connection attempt if domain name resolution fails, such as when the DNS server indicates that it can't resolve the domain, responds with a redirection to a different server, or fails to respond (timeout).
* 'NeverConnect': The specified domains should never trigger a VPN connection attempt.

subkeys.title: Required DNS Servers
subkeys.content:
An array of IP addresses of DNS servers to use for resolving the specified domains. These servers don't need to be part of the device's current network configuration. If these DNS servers aren't reachable, the system establishes a VPN connection. These DNS servers need to be either internal DNS servers or trusted external DNS servers.
This key is valid only if the value of 'DomainAction' is 'ConnectIfNeeded'.

subkeys.title: Required URL String Probe
subkeys.content:
An HTTP or HTTPS (preferred) URL to probe, using a GET request. If the URL's hostname can't be resolved, if the server is unreachable, or if the server doesn't respond with a 200 HTTP status code, a VPN connection is established in response.
This key is valid only if the value of 'DomainAction' is 'ConnectIfNeeded'.

subkeys.title: DNS Domain Match
subkeys.content:
An array of domain names. This rule matches if any of the domain names in the specified list matches any domain in the device's search domains list.
The system supports a wildcard (`*`) prefix. For example, `*.example.com` matches against either `mydomain.example.com` or `yourdomain.example.com`.

subkeys.title: DNS Server Address Match
subkeys.content:
An array of IP addresses. This rule matches if any of the network's specified DNS servers match any entry in the array.
The system supports matching with a single wildcard. For example, `17.*` matches any DNS server in the `17.0.0.0/8` subnet.

subkeys.title: Interface Type Match
subkeys.content: An interface type. If specified, this rule matches only if the primary network interface hardware matches the specified type.

subkeys.title: SSID Match
subkeys.content:
An array of SSIDs to match against the current network. If the network isn't a Wi-Fi network or if the SSID doesn't appear in this array, the match fails.
Omit this key and the corresponding array to match against any SSID.

subkeys.title: URL String Probe
subkeys.content: A URL to probe. This rule matches when this URL is successfully fetched (returns a `200` HTTP status code) without redirection. Not available in watchOS.

subkeys.title: PayloadCertificateUUID
subkeys.content:
The UUID of the identity certificate as the account credential. If `AuthenticationMethod` is `Certificate`, and extended authentication (EAP) isn't used, this certificate is sent out for IKE client authentication. If extended authentication is used, this certificate can be used for EAP-TLS.

Available in macOS 14 and later.

subkeys.title: Account Password
subkeys.content:
The password to use for the account credentials. Only used if `AuthenticationMethod` is `Password`.

Available in macOS 14 and later.

subkeys.title: Provider Bundle Identifier
subkeys.content:
If the VPNSubType field contains the bundle identifier of an app that contains multiple VPN providers of the same type (app-proxy or packet-tunnel), then the system uses this field to choose which provider to use for this configuration. If the VPN provider is implemented as a System Extension, then this field is required.

Available in macOS 14 and later.

subkeys.title: Provider Designated Requirement
subkeys.content:
If the VPN provider is implemented as a System Extension, then this field is required.

Available in macOS 14 and later.

subkeys.title: ProviderType
subkeys.content:
If the value of this key is `app-proxy`, the VPN service tunnels traffic at the application layer. If the value of this key is `packet-tunnel`, the VPN service tunnels traffic at the IP layer.

Available in macOS 14 and later.

subkeys.title: Order
subkeys.content:
A positive integer.

Available in macOS 14 and later.

payloads.title: Web Clip
payloads.description: The profile that configures web clips on the device.

keys.title: Precomposed Icon
keys.content: If `true`, the system prevents SpringBoard from adding shine to the icon.

keys.title: Full Screen
keys.content: If `true`, the system launches the web clip as a full-screen web app.

keys.title: URL
keys.content: The URL of the web clip.

keys.title: Icon
keys.content: The PNG icon to show on the Home Screen. If not set, the system displays a white square. For best results, provide a square image that's no larger than 400 x 400 pixels and less than 1 MB when uncompressed. The graphics file is automatically scaled and cropped to fit, if necessary, and converted to PNG format. Web clip icons are 144 x 144 pixels for iPad devices with a Retina display, and 114 x 114 pixels for iPhone devices. To prevent the device from adding a shine to the image, set `Precomposed` to `true`.

keys.title: Removable
keys.content: If `true`, the system enables removing the web clip.

keys.title: Label
keys.content: The name of the web clip that the system displays on the Home Screen.

keys.title: Ignore Web Clip manifest scope
keys.content: If `true`, a full screen web clip can navigate to an external web site without showing Safari UI. Otherwise, Safari UI appears when navigating away from the web clip's URL. This key has no effect when `FullScreen` is `false`. Available in iOS 14 and later.

keys.title: Target Application Bundle Identifier
keys.content: The application bundle identifier of the application that opens the URL. To use this property, install the profile through MDM. Available in iOS 14 and later.

payloads.title: Web Content Filter
payloads.description: The payload that configures web content filters.

keys.title: FilterType
keys.content: The type of filter, built-in or plug-in. In macOS, the system only supports the plug-in value.

keys.title: SafariHistoryRetentionEnabled
keys.content: If `true`, this payload enforces a policy which requires retention of browsing history. This causes Safari to disable clearing of browsing history, and prevents the use of private browsing mode because that mode doesn't keep browsing history.

keys.title: Web filter enabled
keys.content: If `true`, the system enables automatic filtering. Use when `FilterType` is `BuiltIn`.

keys.title: PermittedURLs
keys.content: An array or URLs that are accessible whether or not the automatic filter allows access. Use when `FilterType` is `BuiltIn`. Requires that `AutoFilterEnabled` is `true`.

keys.title: BlacklistedURLs
keys.content: Use `DenyListURLs` instead.

keys.title: DenyListURLs
keys.content: An array of URLs that are inaccessible. Use when `FilterType` is `BuiltIn`. Limit the number of these URLs to no more than 500.

keys.title: HideDenyListURLs
keys.content: If `true`, the device hides the `DenyListURLs` item in the profiles that display in Settings > General > VPN & Device Management.

keys.title: White list
keys.content: Use `AllowListBookmarks` instead.

subkeys.title: URL
subkeys.content: The URL of the bookmark in the allow list.

subkeys.title: Title
subkeys.content: The title of the bookmark.

keys.title: Allow list
keys.content: An array of dictionaries that define the pages that the user can bookmark or visit. Use when `FilterType` is `BuiltIn`.

subkeys.title: URL
subkeys.content: The URL of the bookmark in the allow list.

subkeys.title: Title
subkeys.content: The title of the bookmark.

keys.title: UserDefinedName
keys.content: The display name for this filtering configuration. Required when `FilterType` is `Plugin`.

keys.title: PluginBundleID
keys.content: The bundle ID of the plug-in that provides filtering service. Required when `FilterType` is `Plugin`. Otherwise, it ignores this value. Consult your filtering solution vendor to determine what to specify for this value. Required when `FilterType` is `Plugin`.

keys.title: ServerAddress
keys.content: The server address, which may be the IP address, hostname, or URL. Use when `FilterType` is `Plugin`.

keys.title: Username
keys.content: The user name for the service. Use when `FilterType` is `Plugin`.

keys.title: Password
keys.content: The password for the service. Use when `FilterType` is `Plugin`.

keys.title: Certificate UUID
keys.content: The UUID of the certificate payload within the same profile that the system uses to authenticate the user. Use when `FilterType` is `Plugin`.

keys.title: Organization
keys.content: The organization string to pass to the third-party plug-in. Use when `FilterType` is `Plugin`.

keys.title: VendorConfig
keys.content: The custom dictionary that the filtering service plug-in needs. Use when `FilterType` is `Plugin`.

subkeys.title: ANY
subkeys.content: The custom key/value pairs for the filtering service.

keys.title: FilterBrowsers
keys.content:
If `true`, the system enables filtering WebKit traffic. Use when `FilterType` is `Plugin`.

> Note:
> At least one of `FilterBrowsers` or `FilterSockets` needs to be `true`.

keys.title: FilterSockets
keys.content:
If `true`, enables the filtering of socket traffic. Use when `FilterType` is `Plugin`.

> Note:
> At least one of `FilterBrowsers` or `FilterSockets` needs to be `true`.

keys.title: Filter Data Provider Designated Requirement
keys.content: The designated requirement string that the system embeds in the code signature of the filter data provider system extension. This string identifies the filter data provider when the filter starts running. Required if `FilterSockets` is `true`.

keys.title: Filter Data Provider Bundle Identifier
keys.content: The bundle identifier string of the filter data provider system extension. This string identifies the filter data provider when the filter starts running. Required if `FilterSockets` is `true`.

keys.title: Filter Network Packets
keys.content:
If `true` and `FilterType` is `Plugin`, the system enables filtering network packets. Use when `FilterType` is `Plugin`.

> Note:
> At least one of `FilterPackets` or `FilterSockets` needs to be `true`.

keys.title: Filter Packet Provider Designated Requirement
keys.content: The designated requirement string that the system embeds in the code signature of the filter packet provider system extension. This string identifies the filter packet provider when the filter starts running. Required if `FilterPackets` is `true`.

keys.title: Filter Packet Provider Bundle Identifier
keys.content: The bundle identifier string of the filter packet provider system extension. This string identifies the filter packet provider when the filter starts running. Required if `FilterPackets` is `true`.

keys.title: Filter Grade
keys.content: The system uses this value to derive the relative order of content filters. Filters with a grade of `firewall` see network traffic before filters with a grade of `inspector`. However, the system doesn't define the order of filters within a grade.

keys.title: Content Filter UUID
keys.content: A globally unique identifier for this content filter configuration. The content filter processes network traffic for managed apps with the same `ContentFilterUUID` in their app attributes. Use when `FilterType` is `Plugin`.This key must be present for unsupervised devices and user enrollment.

keys.title: FilterURLs
keys.content: If `true`, the system filters URL requests. Use when `FilterType` is `Plugin`. Available in iOS 26 and macOS 26, and later.

keys.title: URLFilterParameters
keys.content: A dictionary containing URL filter parameters. Required when `FilterURLs` is `true`. Available in iOS 26 and macOS 26 and later.

subkeys.title: URL Filter Control Provider Designated Requirement
subkeys.content: The designated requirement string in the code signature of the URL filter control provider app extension. The system uses this string to identify the URL filter control provider when the filter starts running. Required in macOS.

subkeys.title: URL Filter Control Provider Bundle Identifier
subkeys.content: The bundle identifier string of the URL filter control provider app extension. The system uses this string to identify the URL filter control provider when the filter starts running.

subkeys.title: Private Information Retrieval server URL
subkeys.content: The URL containing the domain name of the private information retrieval server.

subkeys.title: Privacy Pass Issuer URL
subkeys.content: The URL containing the domain name of Privacy Pass Issuer.

subkeys.title: Authentication Token
subkeys.content: The per-user authentication token string, which is an HTTP bearer token for the person using your app. The system uses this token to attest that it is a valid user when requesting anonymous authentication tokens for PIR exchanges.

subkeys.title: URLFilterFailClosed
subkeys.content: If `true`, the system blocks URLs if the filter is enabled, but it fails to make any filtering decision; for example, if there's a communication failure with the PIR server. If `false`, the system allows URLs if the filter is enabled, but it fails to make any filtering decision.

subkeys.title: URLPrefilterFetchFrequency
subkeys.content: The time interval in seconds that the system uses to periodically run the `NEURLFilterControlProvider` app extension. The default value is 86400 seconds (1 day). The minimum allowed value is 2700 seconds (45 minutes). The system allows `NEURLFilterControlProvider` implementations to download prefilter Bloom filter data onto the device periodically at the specified interval. Implementations need to allow for a slight difference between the scheduled time and the actual runtime of the task, due to the scheduling mechanism on the system.

payloads.title: Wi-Fi
payloads.description: The payload that configures Wi-Fi settings.

keys.title: Auto Join
keys.content:
If `true`, the device joins the network automatically.

If `false`, the user must tap the network name to join it.

keys.title: SSID
keys.content: The SSID of the Wi-Fi network to use. In iOS 7.0 and later, the SSID is optional if a value exists for `DomainName` value.

keys.title: Hidden
keys.content: If `true`, defines this network as hidden.

keys.title: Proxy Type
keys.content: The proxy type, if any, to use. If you choose the manual proxy type, you need the proxy server address, including its port and optionally a user name and password into the proxy server. If you choose the auto proxy type, you can enter a proxy autoconfiguration (PAC) URL.

keys.title: Encryption Type
keys.content:
The encryption type for the network.

If set to anything except `None`, the payload may contain the following three keys: `Password`, `PayloadCertificateUUID`, or `EAPClientConfiguration`.

As of iOS 16, tvOS 16, watchOS 9, and macOS 13:

- `WPA` allows joining WPA or WPA2 networks
- `WPA2` allows joining WPA2 or WPA3 networks
- `WPA3` allows joining WPA3 networks only
- `Any` allows joining WPA, WPA2, WPA3, and WEP networks

Prior to iOS 16, tvOS 16, and watchOS 9, specifying `WPA`, `WPA2`, and `WPA3` were equivalent and would allow joining any WPA network.

Prior to macOS 13, the encryption type, if specified explicitly, needed to match the encryption type of the network exactly.

keys.title: Password
keys.content: The password for the access point.

keys.title: Certificate UUID
keys.content: The UUID of the certificate payload within the same profile to use for the client credential.

keys.title: EAP Client Configuration
keys.content: The enterprise network configuration.

subkeys.title: Accept EAP Types
subkeys.content:
The EAP types that the system accepts. Allowed values:

- `13`: EAP-TLS
- `17`: LEAP
- `18`: EAP-SIM
- `21`: EAP-TTLS
- `23`: EAP-AKA
- `25`: PEAPv0/v1
- `43`: EAP-FAST

For EAP-TLS authentication without a network payload, install the necessary identity certificates and have your users select EAP-TLS mode in the 802.1X credentials dialog that appears when they connect to the network. For other EAP types, a network payload is necessary and must specify the correct settings for the network.

subkeys.title: Username
subkeys.content: The user name for the account. If you don't specify a value, the system prompts the user during login.

subkeys.title: Password
subkeys.content: The user's password. If you don't specify a value, the system prompts the user during login.

subkeys.title: Certificate Anchor UUID
subkeys.content: An array of the UUID of each certificate payload in the same profile to trust for authentication. Use this key to prevent the device from asking the user whether to trust the listed certificates. Dynamic trust (the certificate dialogue) is in a disabled state if you specify this property without also enabling 'TLSAllowTrustExceptions'.

subkeys.title: TLS Trusted Certificates
subkeys.content: An array of trusted certificates. Each entry in the array must contain certificate data that represents an anchor certificate used for verifying the server certificate.

subkeys.title: TLSTrustedCertificatesItem
subkeys.content: A certificate identifier.

subkeys.title: TLS Trusted Server Names
subkeys.content:
The list of accepted server certificate common names. If a server presents a certificate that isn't in this list, the system doesn't trust it.
If you specify this property, the system disables dynamic trust (the certificate dialog) unless you also specify 'TLSAllowTrustExceptions' with the value 'true'.
If necessary, use wildcards to specify the name, such as 'wpa.*.example.com'.

subkeys.title: Allow Trust Exceptions
subkeys.content:
If 'true', allows a dynamic trust decision by the user. The dynamic trust is the certificate dialogue that appears when the system doesn't trust a certificate.
If 'false', the authentication fails if the system doesn't already trust the certificate.
As of iOS 8, Apple no longer supports this key.

subkeys.title: TLSCertificateIsRequired
subkeys.content:
If 'true', allows for two-factor authentication for EAP-TTLS, PEAP, or EAP-FAST. If 'false', allows for zero-factor authentication for EAP-TLS.
If you don't specify a value, the default is 'true' for EAP-TLS, and 'false' for other EAP types.

subkeys.title: TTLS Inner Authentication
subkeys.content: The inner authentication that the TTLS module uses.

subkeys.title: TLSMinimumVersion
subkeys.content: The minimum TLS version for EAP authentication.

subkeys.title: TLSMaximumVersion
subkeys.content: The maximum TLS version for EAP authentication.

subkeys.title: Outer Identity
subkeys.content:
A name that hides the user's true name. The user's actual name appears only inside the encrypted tunnel. For example, you might set this to anonymous or anon, or anon@mycompany.net. It can increase security because an attacker can't see the authenticating user's name in the clear.
This key is only relevant to TTLS, PEAP, and EAP-FAST.
This field is required if 'TLSMinimumVersion' is '1.3'.

subkeys.title: Use PAC
subkeys.content: If 'true', the device uses an existing PAC if it's present. Otherwise, the server must present its identity using a certificate.

subkeys.title: Provision PAC
subkeys.content:
If 'true', allows PAC provisioning.

This value is only applicable if 'EAPFASTUsePAC' is 'true'. This value must be 'true' for EAP-FAST PAC usage to succeed because there's no other way to provision a PAC.

subkeys.title: Provision PAC Anonymously
subkeys.content: If 'true', provisions the device anonymously. Note that there are known machine-in-the-middle attacks for anonymous provisioning.

subkeys.title: Allow Two RANDs
subkeys.content:
The minimum number of RAND values to accept from the server.
For use with EAP-SIM only.

subkeys.title: SystemModeCredentialsSource
subkeys.content:
Set this string to 'ActiveDirectory' to use the AD computer name and password credentials.
If using this property, you can't use 'SystemModeUseOpenDirectoryCredentials'.

subkeys.title: SystemModeUseOpenDirectoryCredentials
subkeys.content:
If 'true', the system mode connection tries to use the Open Directory credentials.
If using this property, you can't use 'SystemModeCredentialsSource'.

subkeys.title: Per-Connection Password
subkeys.content: If 'true', the user receives a prompt for a password each time they connect to the network.

keys.title: Displayed Operator Name
keys.content: The operator name to display when connected to this network. Used only with Wi-Fi Hotspot 2.0 access points.

keys.title: Domain Name
keys.content: The primary domain of the tunnel.

keys.title: Roaming OIs
keys.content: An array of Roaming Consortium Organization Identifiers used for Wi-Fi Hotspot 2.0 negotiation.

keys.title: Roaming Enable
keys.content: If `true`, allows connection to roaming service providers.

keys.title: Is Hotspot
keys.content: If `true`, the device treats the network as a hotspot.

keys.title: HESSID
keys.content: The HESSID used for Wi-Fi Hotspot 2.0 negotiation.

keys.title: Realm Names
keys.content: An array of Network Access Identifier Realm names used for Wi-Fi Hotspot 2.0 negotiation.

keys.title: MCC/MNCs
keys.content: An array of Mobile Country Code/Mobile Network Code (MCC/MNC) pairs used for Wi-Fi Hotspot 2.0 negotiation. Each string must contain exactly six digits.

keys.title: Disable Captive Network Detection
keys.content: If `true`, the system bypasses Captive Network detection when the device connects to the network.

keys.title: QoS Marking Policy
keys.content: A dictionary that contains the list of apps that the system allows to benefit from L2 and L3 marking. When this dictionary isn't present, the system allows all apps to use L2 and L3 marking when the Wi-Fi network supports Cisco QoS fast lane.

subkeys.title: Allowlisted App Identifiers
subkeys.content: An array of app bundle identifiers that defines the allow list for L2 and L3 marking for traffic that goes to the Wi-Fi network. If the array isn't present, but the `QoSMarkingPolicy` key is present — even empty — no apps can use L2 and L3 marking.

subkeys.title: Whitelisted App Identifiers
subkeys.content: Use `QoSMarkingAllowListAppIdentifiers` instead.

subkeys.title: QoS marking for audio or video calls
subkeys.content: If `true`, adds audio and video traffic of built-in audio or video services, such as FaceTime and Wi-Fi Calling, to the allow list for L2 and L3 marking for traffic that goes to the Wi-Fi network.

subkeys.title: Allow QoS marking
subkeys.content:
If `true`, disables L3 marking and only uses L2 marking for traffic that goes to the Wi-Fi network.



If `false`, the system behaves as if Wi-Fi doesn't have an association with a Cisco QoS fast lane network.

keys.title: SetupModes
keys.content: An array of strings that contain the type of connection mode to attach.

subkeys.title: SetupModesItem
subkeys.content: A type of connection mode.

keys.title: EnableIPv6
keys.content: If `true`, enables IPv6 on this interface.

keys.title: Certificate Required
keys.content: If `true`, allows for two-factor authentication for EAP-TTLS, PEAP, or EAP-FAST. If `false`, allows for zero-factor authentication for EAP-TLS.

keys.title: Proxy Server
keys.content: The proxy server's network address.

keys.title: Proxy Server Port
keys.content: The proxy server's port number.

keys.title: Proxy Username
keys.content: The user name used to authenticate to the proxy server.

keys.title: Proxy Password
keys.content: The password used to authenticate to the proxy server.

keys.title: Proxy PAC URL
keys.content: The URL of the PAC file that defines the proxy configuration.

keys.title: Proxy PAC Fallback Allowed
keys.content: If `true`, allows connecting directly to the destination if the PAC file is unreachable.

keys.title: Disable MAC address randomization during association
keys.content:
If `true,` disables MAC address randomization for a Wi-Fi network while associated with that network. This feature also shows a privacy warning in Settings indicating that the network has reduced privacy protections.

If `false`, then the system enables MAC address randomization on iOS, watchOS, and visionOS.

This value is only locked when MDM installs the profile. If the profile is manually installed, the system sets the value but the user can change it.

keys.title: Allow Join Before First Unlock
keys.content:
If `true`, the device makes this network available for joining before the device is unlocked for the first time following a reboot, on a device configured for return to service. Any network credentials are placed into Class D storage within the keychain, and information about the network is stored on disk in Class D.

There are several restrictions on the use of this flag:

- This property is only available in the return to service mode.
- Only one network can be designated as available before first unlock.
- `EAPClientConfiguration` must not be present.
- If `IsHotspot` is present, it must be set to `false`.
- `QoSMarkingPolicy` must not be present.
- If `ProxyType` is present, it must be set to `None`.

The device fails to install the profile payload if any of these conditions are not met.

payloads.title: Wi-Fi Managed Settings
payloads.description: The payload that configures managed Wi-Fi settings.

keys.title: RequireAdminForIBSS
keys.content: If `true`, requires administrator authorization to enable IBSS.

keys.title: RequireAdminForAirPortNetworkChange
keys.content: If `true`, requires administrator authorization for network changes.

keys.title: RequireAdminToTurnAirPortOnOff
keys.content: If `true`, requires administrator authorization to turn Wi-Fi on or off.

payloads.title: Xsan
payloads.description: The payload that configures an Xsan client system.

keys.title: sanName
keys.content: The name of the SAN. This key is required for all Xsan SANs. The name must exactly match the name of the SAN defined in the metadata server.

keys.title: sanConfigURLs
keys.content:
An array of LDAP URLs where Xsan systems can obtain SAN configuration updates. There should be one entry for each Xsan MDC.

This key is required for all Xsan SANs.

Example URL: `ldaps://mdc1.example.com:389`.

subkeys.title: sanConfigURLsItem
subkeys.content: A URL.

keys.title: fsnameservers
keys.content:
An array of storage area network (SAN) File System Name Server coordinators. The list should contain the same addresses in the same order as the metadata controller (MDC) `/Library/Preferences/Xsan/fsnameservers` file.

This key is required for StorNext SANs.

subkeys.title: fsnameserversItem
subkeys.content: A name server.

keys.title: sanAuthMethod
keys.content:
The authentication method for the SAN. This key is required for all Xsan SANs. It's optional for StorNext SANs but should be set if the StorNext SAN uses an `auth_secret` file.



Only one value is accepted: `auth_secret`

keys.title: sharedSecret
keys.content: The shared secret used for Xsan network authentication. This key is required when the `sanAuthMethod` key is present. The value should equal the content of the MDC's `/Library/Preferences/Xsan/.auth_secret` file.

payloads.title: Xsan Preferences
payloads.description: The payload that configures the Xsan preferences that define the volumes that automatically mount at startup.

keys.title: onlyMount
keys.content: An array of Xsan or StorNext volume names. The Xsan client attempts to automatically mount these volumes at startup. The system administrator can mount additional volumes manually by using the `xsanctl(8)` mount command.

subkeys.title: onlyMountItem
subkeys.content: A volume name.

keys.title: denyMount
keys.content: An array of Xsan or StorNext volume names. If no `onlyMount` array is present, the Xsan client automatically attempts to mount all SAN volumes except the volumes in this array. The system administrator can mount those volumes manually by using the `xsanctl(8)` mount command.

subkeys.title: denyMountItem
subkeys.content: A volume name.

keys.title: denyDLC
keys.content: An array of StorNext volume names. If the Xsan client is attempting to mount a volume named in this array, the client only mounts the volume if its logical units (LUNs) are available through Fibre Channel. It doesn't attempt to mount the volume using Distributed LAN Client (DLC).

subkeys.title: denyDLCItem
subkeys.content: A volume name.

keys.title: preferDLC
keys.content: An array of StorNext volume names. If the Xsan client is attempting to mount a volume named in this array, the Xsan client attempts to mount the volume using DLC. If DLC isn't available, the client attempts to mount the volume if its LUNs are available through Fibre Channel. The volume name must not also appear in `denyDLC`.

subkeys.title: preferDLCItem
subkeys.content: A volume name.

keys.title: useDLC
keys.content: If `true`, use the DLC for all volumes.
